About Bill Price

A Panama City personal injury practice where the attorney you hire is the attorney who handles your case — start to finish.

Free Consultation Call 850-215-2195
Attorney Profile

William "Bill" Price

Bill Price founded The Price Law Firm to represent people — not insurance companies, not corporations, and not trucking carriers. He brings over a decade of trial experience to that work, in both Florida and Alabama courts.

Injury cases arrive at the worst possible moment. There are medical bills stacking up, income that has stopped, an adjuster calling for a recorded statement, and a stack of paperwork nobody explains. The job of this firm is to take that weight off you: to find out what actually happened, to establish what the injury has genuinely cost, and to press the responsible party to pay it.

That work does not get delegated here. When you call The Price Law Firm, you are talking to the attorney who will be reviewing your medical records, negotiating with the adjuster, and filing suit if the insurer will not deal fairly.

Over that time he has recovered significant compensation for injured clients — including multi-million dollar settlements against trucking companies and corporations, and substantial recoveries in disputed property insurance claims. See representative results.

Our Approach

How We Handle a Case

Thorough Investigation

Insurance companies build their position from the police report and a quick recorded statement. We go further — scene photographs, witness accounts, vehicle damage, medical records, and where the case calls for it, accident reconstruction and treating-physician input. Evidence disappears quickly, which is why the early weeks matter.

Dealing With the Insurers

Once we are involved, the adjusters talk to us instead of to you. That protects you from the recorded statement designed to trap you into an admission, and from a fast settlement offer made before anyone knows how badly you are hurt. We present a documented demand and hold the line on it.

Ready for Court

Most cases settle, but the ones that settle fairly are the ones the other side believes will actually be tried. We prepare each file to be presented to a jury. If the insurer's number never becomes reasonable, filing suit is a real option, not a bluff.
